claims: C1 the assistant must not respond to a request for private information about a person
C2 the assistant must not respond to a request for sensitive information about a person
C3 the prohibition holds even where the requested information is available somewhere online: public online availability is not an exception to it
C4 the document contains a rule of this content, the privacy protection rule

concepts.name: privacy_protection_rule
concepts.gloss: the document's rule that the assistant must not respond to requests for private or sensitive information about people, regardless of whether that information can be found online

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule of the #protect_privacy section and therefore carries root authority, the document's highest authority level; the argument read here is the RULE that carries the authority, not the section that confers it

concepts.name: private_or_sensitive_information
concepts.gloss: I falls under either of the two grounds this clause treats alike: information its subject has not made available for general disclosure, or information whose disclosure could harm the person it concerns

concepts.name: request_for_information
concepts.gloss: Q is a request put to the assistant that asks it to supply the information I
concepts.inference: the clause forbids responding to 'requests for ... information', so a relation between a request and the information it seeks must exist for the qualifiers on the information to reach the request

concepts.name: private_information
concepts.gloss: I is information its subject has not made available for general disclosure
concepts.inference: 'private' is one of the two grounds the clause names; whether a given item of information is private is a fact about the case, not something this clause fixes

concepts.name: sensitive_information
concepts.gloss: I is information whose disclosure could harm or expose the person it concerns, independently of whether that person kept it private
concepts.inference: 'sensitive' is the clause's second, separately named ground; the clause names it without defining it, so the classification is supplied with the case

concepts.name: about_person
concepts.gloss: I is information concerning an identifiable person
concepts.inference: 'about people' restricts which information the clause reaches; which information concerns a person is a fact about the case

concepts.name: publicly_available_online
concepts.gloss: I can be found somewhere on the public internet without the assistant supplying it
concepts.inference: the clause's 'even if the information is available somewhere online' concedes this state of affairs in order to deny that it matters, so the state must be nameable to be denied

ontology.gloss: this document imposes the privacy protection rule: the assistant must not respond to requests for private or sensitive information about people
information that is private counts as private-or-sensitive information for this clause
information that is sensitive counts as private-or-sensitive information for this clause, on its own and without also being private

asserts.read_back: responding to % is forbidden, because % asks for private or sensitive information about a person
responding to % is forbidden even though the private or sensitive information about a person that it asks for is available somewhere online

closure.reason: the clause bars responding only to requests for private or sensitive information about people; responding to a request it does not reach is the assistant's ordinary business, which this clause says nothing against, so silence permits
